title: Settlement, sincerity, and limits of forbearance
shortTitle: Settlement, sincerity, and limits of forbearance
summary: The notes examine the tradeoff between settling uncertainty and protecting bad-faith assertions.
notes: A later determination that a claim lacked merit differs from knowledge of its invalidity when the bargain was made. The paternity example illustrates this timing. Litigation certification rules, community agreements, and other forms of waiver raise distinct constraints. The Dyer remand means the alleged promise and belief still require proof; it does not establish a valid lifetime-employment bargain on the pleadings alone.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 67–68. Open assigned page 67.
